jobs.description: WHO YOU'LL WORK WITH EMEA Brand Planning and Operations (BPO) is the operating system of Nike Marketing. We connect Global, Geo and Territory teams through planning and operational excellence, enabling world-class marketing to land efficiently and on time. This role reports to the Director, Planning & Operations, Marketplace & Media. It plays a critical role in supporting Retail Brand Marketing across EMEA, helping bring seasonal brand strategies to life within the marketplace. This role leads Marketplace Planning & Operations for Retail Marketing. It translates seasonal and seasonless priorities into integrated plans, guiding teams through key gates and milestones, and ensuring readiness across owned and partner retail channels. You will partner with EMEA BPO, Sport Planning & Operations, Retail Marketing leadership, Retail Experiences, Marketing Finance, Marketplace teams, Territory partners and Global Retail Planning & Operations. You will connect seasonal intent with marketplace execution, budgets and operational readiness, building trusted relationships that help teams navigate decisions, dependencies, risks and delivery. WHO WE ARE LOOKING FOR We are looking for an experienced program and process management professional who brings structure to a fast-moving matrix, combines rigorous planning with clear decision-making, and is motivated by simplifying ways of working so teams can focus on delivering impactful marketing work. You’ll bring business operations experience and understand how marketing and retail organizations translate strategy into execution. You are comfortable proactively identifying risks, connecting work across teams and seasons, and driving alignment through clear communication and governance. You are organized, detail-oriented and collaborative, with the ability to dive deep into operational details while communicating insights and recommendations clearly to senior leaders. You’ll bring: Experience leading program, portfolio, project or business operations experience in a complex, matrixed organization. Proven ability to run end-to-end operating rhythms, integrated plans and critical paths across multiple workstreams. Strong process management skills, including workflow design and continuous improvement. Confidence using data and scenarios to identify risks early and recommend action. Experience supporting budget planning, forecasting, tracking and reporting. Excellent stakeholder management and concise executive communication in English. Strong attention to detail, proactive problem solving and enterprise thinking. Proficiency with Microsoft Office, Keynote, Smartsheet and AirTable. WHAT YOU'LL WORK ON You will lead seasonal and seasonless planning and operations work that enables Retail Marketing to deliver with precision across marketplace readiness, governance, communication, budgets and execution. You will: Lead seasonal readiness across EMEA Retail Marketing, guiding teams through key planning gates, milestones and deliverables to ensure plans are launched on time and with clarity. Own integrated program plans, critical paths, connecting priorities, dependencies, owners, decisions and timelines across Retail Marketing, Marketplace and Territory teams. Maintain and continuously improve marketplace planning tools, templates and operating processes, simplifying ways of working and strengthening adoption across the organization. Own the accuracy of key planning artefacts, ensuring teams have a trusted source of truth for execution decisions. Translate complex information into clear updates, communications and leadership-ready reporting that drive alignment and action. Partner with Marketing Finance to support budget excellence. Applications will be accepted until Friday, October 9th. We encourage external candidates to apply as soon as possible, as the posting may close earlier if we receive a sufficient number of applications.

In this role, you’ll help us deliver better care for billions of people around the world. It starts with YOU. As a Maintenance Parts Coordinator, you'll join a team helping build one of the industry's most advanced manufacturing operations. In this role, you'll help keep a world-class facility running by ensuring critical maintenance parts and supplies are available when they are needed most. You'll partner closely with maintenance, operations, and suppliers to solve problems, minimize downtime, and support equipment reliability. Through inventory planning, data analysis, and continuous improvement, you'll help drive operational performance while balancing service, cost, and inventory health. It starts with YOU. Manage the procurement and replenishment of Maintenance, Repair, and Operations (MRO) parts, supplies, and spare components to support plant operations. Monitor material requirements planning (MRP) activity to ensure parts and supplies are available when needed for production, maintenance, and planned shutdowns. Coordinate with suppliers and internal customers to expedite urgent orders, communicate delivery updates, and resolve supply chain issues. Support machine reliability by quickly sourcing and securing parts during equipment breakdowns and emergency situations. Analyze inventory health metrics, material usage trends, and stocking strategies to improve inventory performance and reduce shortages. Manage material master data and inventory records within SAP, including new material setup, changes, and inventory transactions. Lead or support refurbishment programs, obsolete inventory reviews, and continuous improvement efforts to maximize asset value and inventory efficiency. Partner with maintenance, operations, procurement, and storeroom teams to ensure materials are available to meet production and reliability objectives. Promote a safe, organized, and efficient storeroom environment through cycle counting, inventory accuracy, housekeeping, and continuous improvement activities. Proficiency with Microsoft Office (Excel, Word, and PowerPoint). Experience utilizing SAP or similar ERP systems, with strong attention to detail and the ability to manage purchasing, inventory, and material transactions accurately. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to build effective working relationships, collaborate across functions, provide timely updates, drive effective problem resolution, and inform, engage, and influence a diverse range of internal and external partners. For a complete overview, see www.mykcbenefits.com ​ Great support for good health with medical, dental, and vision coverage options with no waiting periods or pre-existing condition restrictions. Access to an on-site fitness center, occupational health nurse, and allowances for high-quality safety equipment. Flexible Savings and spending accounts to maximize health care options and stretch dollars when caring for yourself or dependents. 회사 소개
쿠팡은 고객 감동 실현을 위해 존재합니다. 고객들이 "쿠팡 없이 그동안 어떻게 살았을까?" 라고 말할 때, 비로소 우리의 미션을 실현하고 있음을 알 수 있습니다. 고객들의 쇼핑과 식사, 생활 전반을 편하게 만들겠다는 유일한 집념으로 쿠팡은 수억 달러 규모의 이커머스 산업 전반의 혁신을 이끌고 있습니다. 쿠팡은 가장 빠르게 성장하는 이커머스 기업 중 하나로, 국내 커머스 업계에서의 독보적인 입지와, 고객 신뢰를 구축했습니다.
쿠팡은 스타트업 문화를 기반으로 한 글로벌 대형 상장사라고 자부합니다. 이것이 창립 당시의 기민함을 지하며, 신규 서비스를 끊임없이 출시하며 비즈니스를 확장해 나가는 우리의 성장 동력입니다. 쿠팡의 모든 임직원에게는 기업가 정신을 갖추고 새로운 혁신과 이니셔티브를 추진할 수 있는 기회가 주어집니다. 주저 없이 일에 뛰어들어 성과를 이루고자 하는 과감성이, 바로 쿠팡이 일하는 방식의 본질입니다. 쿠팡에서는 여러분 자신, 동료, 팀 그리고 회사 전체가 매일 성장하는 모습을 목격할 것입니다.
쿠팡의 모든 직원은 커머스의 미래를 만들겠다는 쿠팡의 미션에 진심입니다. 우리는 고객의 문제를 해결해 나가고, 전통적인 관념과 통념에 맞서며 실현 가능한 한계를 뛰어넘고 있습니다. 고가용성 (always-on) 과 최첨단의 앞선 기술 (high-tech), 초연결사회 (hyper-connected world) 에서의 놀라운 업무 경험을 원하신다면, 지금 바로 쿠팡에 합류하세요.

About the Team
Producers at DoorDash, Deliveroo, Wolt, and 7Rooms are strategic and creative problem solvers, crafting scalable solutions that empower transformative and high-quality design. By driving innovation and excellence, they play a key role in shaping the future of Design at our companies, making a lasting impact on our community and beyond.
About the Role
Studio Central is a global team within Studio, DoorDash's Product Design organization, supporting DoorDash, Wolt, Deliveroo, and 7Rooms. We own how brand shows up in the product experience, partnering closely with Marketing and Product teams to shape cohesive, high-quality work and to help define the foundations, vision, and future state of design across our portfolio. Our work spans major brand moments, merchandising, and the systems that connect it all.
There's no finished playbook here, and that's intentional. As the Staff Producer for Studio Central, we're looking for someone who thrives building structure from scratch: getting our design standards documented, adopted, and evolving across every brand and surface, and keeping work moving from brief to delivery across in-house teams, agencies, and cross-functional partners in Product Design, Marketing, and Engineering. You'll help build Studio Central's operating model as we go, setting the standard for how a distributed design organization stays aligned as it scales.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
Anthropic is building AI compute at a scale and pace that outruns what off-the-shelf data center equipment was designed for. Much of the power and cooling equipment behind our next campuses — battery energy storage systems (BESS), grid-forming and grid-following inverters, solid-state transformers (SST), E-STATCOM and other power-quality devices, medium-voltage switchgear, UPS, and liquid-cooling systems — is either new to the market, new to the supplier, or being built at a volume the supplier has never shipped before.
The NPI Engineer owns the path from "the supplier has a design" to "the equipment is qualified, manufacturable at rate, and running reliably on site." You sit between our electrical and mechanical design teams, our supply chain and quality teams, and the supplier's engineering and factory organizations, and you make sure every new product or major variant clears the gates — EVT, DVT, PVT, FAT, SAT — before it is trusted with production load. This is a hands-on role: you will spend real time on supplier factory floors, in test labs, and at site commissioning.
What you'll do
Own the NPI program for each new power or cooling product
(BESS, inverters, SST, E-STATCOM, MV switchgear, UPS, CDUs, chillers) from concept selection through ramp, including the gate schedule, exit criteria, and risk register.
Drive early supplier design engagement:
translate our site requirements (fault current, grid interconnection, harmonic and ride-through requirements, thermal envelopes, footprint, serviceability) into product requirements and specifications the supplier can build to, and negotiate trade-offs with their engineering teams.
Lead DFM/DFT/DFx reviews
with suppliers so designs are manufacturable at the rate we need, testable in the factory, and serviceable in the field.
Plan and run prototype and pilot builds:
define EVT/DVT/PVT scope and sample counts, witness builds, own test plans (type testing, HALT/HASS, thermal, EMC, protection coordination, functional and integration tests), and drive root cause and corrective action on every failure.
Qualify the product for deployment:
define and execute first-article inspection, factory acceptance testing (FAT), site acceptance testing (SAT), and integrated system testing with the rest of the electrical and cooling chain, and sign off on production readiness.
Hand off to steady state:
transfer qualified products, control plans, test procedures, and known-issue lists to the Manufacturing Quality and Supply Chain Delivery teams, and support them through the first production ramps.
Build the reliability picture:
run FMEA/DFMEA with suppliers, define reliability targets and burn-in requirements, and feed field failure data back into the next revision.
Coordinate cross-functionally
with design engineering, construction, commissioning, utilities/interconnection, safety, and sourcing so NPI schedules are integrated with campus delivery schedules.
Keep suppliers honest:
track readiness and risk with clear metrics, escalate early, and hold technical reviews that resolve issues rather than admire them.
You may be a good fit if you have
8+ years of engineering experience in power electronics, electrical equipment, or industrial energy systems, with at least 4 years in an NPI, product development, or product engineering role that owned a product from prototype through production ramp.
Direct, hands-on experience with at least two of: BESS, utility- or data-center-scale inverters, medium-voltage transformers or switchgear, UPS, STATCOM/power-quality equipment, or liquid cooling systems (CDUs, chillers, hydronics).
Working knowledge of the relevant standards and how they get applied in qualification: UL 9540/9540A, UL 1741 and IEEE 1547, IEEE 2800, IEC 62477 / IEC 62909, IEEE C37 and C57 series, NFPA 70/855, UL 1778, and comparable IEC equivalents.
Experience defining and executing structured qualification programs (EVT/DVT/PVT, FAT/SAT, type testing, reliability testing) and closing failures with disciplined root cause analysis and CAPA.
Familiarity with supplier factory environments — production lines, test bays, quality systems — and the ability to assess a supplier's real readiness to ship at rate.
Fluency in design-for-manufacturing and design-for-test principles and the supplier ECO/change-control process.
Strong systems thinking: you can reason about how an inverter, a battery, a transformer, and a cooling loop behave together at a site, not just in isolation.
Clear written and verbal communication, and comfort driving decisions across engineering, supply chain, and executive audiences.
A bachelor's degree in electrical, mechanical, or power engineering, or equivalent experience.
Willingness to travel 30–40% to supplier factories and data center sites, including internationally.
Strong candidates may also have
Experience with solid-state transformers, grid-forming inverters, E-STATCOM, or other emerging power-conversion equipment being introduced to data center or utility applications for the first time.
NPI or product engineering experience at a hyperscaler, a large utility-scale developer, or a Tier-1 power equipment OEM.
Background in grid interconnection studies, protection coordination, or power-system modeling (PSCAD, ETAP, PSS/E, or similar).
Liquid cooling product introduction experience — CDU, rear-door heat exchanger, direct-to-chip, or immersion systems.
Reliability engineering credentials (CRE, Six Sigma) or experience running HALT/HASS programs.
Firmware and controls validation experience for power conversion equipment (inverter control loops, BMS, EMS, PLC/SCADA integration).
Experience standing up or scaling new supplier manufacturing lines, including contract manufacturing and international sites.

Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.

About Anthropic
Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.
About the role
The RL Velocity team owns the efficiency and reliability of our RL Science stack - the infrastructure, tooling, and systems that let researchers iterate quickly on training runs. As a Research Engineer on the team, you'll build and improve the core platform that underpins how we do RL at Anthropic, removing bottlenecks that slow down research and making it easier for the broader org to ship better models faster. This is high-leverage work: small improvements to velocity compound across every researcher and every run.
Responsibilities
Build and improve the RL training infrastructure that researchers depend on day-to-day
Identify and remove bottlenecks across the RL stack: debugging, profiling, and rearchitecting where needed
Partner closely with researchers and with adjacent engineering teams (inference, sandboxing, and many more) to understand pain points and ship tooling that makes them faster
Own the reliability and performance of research runs end-to-end
Contribute to design decisions that shape how Anthropic does RL at scale
You may be a good fit if you
Have strong software engineering fundamentals and a track record of building performant, reliable systems
Have worked on ML infrastructure, distributed systems, or research tooling
Care about enabling other people's work and find leverage through platforms rather than individual experiments
Are comfortable operating across the stack, from low-level performance work to RL algorithms
Have a bias toward shipping and iterating quickly, with a mix of high agency and low ego
Strong candidates may also have
Experience with large-scale distributed training (RL, pre-training, or post-training)
Familiarity with JAX, PyTorch, or similar ML frameworks
A track record of operating at the edge of research and infra in a fast-moving environment

None. Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis.

Visa sponsorship:
We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.
We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification.
Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.
Your safety matters to us.
To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit
anthropic.com/careers
directly for confirmed position openings.
How we're different
We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.
The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.
Come work with us!
Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.

jobs.description: Craft: Technology & Development Job Description: At King, we’re on a mission to make the world playful. The tools, platforms and infrastructure behind our games help teams turn great ideas into experiences enjoyed by millions of players. Engineering System & Support (ESS) builds the shared foundations that make game development smoother: reliable CI/CD, cloud infrastructure, repository services, build tooling and developer workflows. We help teams spend less time waiting on systems and more time creating great games. Your role within the Kingdom As a Senior Systems Engineer (Developer Experience & Infrastructure), you’ll improve the platforms developers rely on every day—making them faster, more reliable and easier to use. What You’ll Do: Elevate Developer Experience: Design, build, and support self-service platform tools and automated workflows that speed up developer feedback loops. Scale Infrastructure: Maintain and modernize our Infrastructure as Code (IaC) and containerized build systems across multi-OS and cloud environments. System Design & Reliability: Shape platform architecture, strengthen monitoring, and troubleshoot complex distributed services. Collaborate & Mentor: Partner closely with game teams across multiple locations, write clear platform documentation, and share knowledge across the engineering community. Skills to create thrills We evaluate candidates based on core capabilities and engineering fundamentals rather than tool-by-tool memorization. Production Linux Expertise: Solid experience managing and troubleshooting Linux systems (e.g., Debian/Ubuntu) in production or high-availability settings. Infrastructure as Code (IaC): Hands-on experience automating infrastructure provisioning using tools like Terraform, Puppet, or similar frameworks. Cloud & Container Orchestration: Practical experience working with major cloud platforms (AWS, GCP, or Azure) and container technologies (Docker, Kubernetes). Automation & Scripting: Proficiency in at least one scripting language (e.g., Bash, Python, Groovy, or PowerShell) to eliminate toil and automate pipelines. Version Control Fundamentals: Solid understanding of Git workflows and modern developer ecosystems. Collaborative Mindset: Strong communication skills, structured task prioritization, and a passion for supporting fellow developers. Managed Services Operations: Experience owning and operating managed services as github.com , artifactory, perforce, builbuddy, buildkite. Bonus Points (Nice to Have, Not Required!) Experience maintaining complex CI/CD pipelines across multi-OS environments (Linux, macOS, Windows). Familiarity with build optimization or repository management tools (e.g., Artifactory, SonarQube, Incredibuild, or Veertu Anka). Exposure to cloud-native monitoring and logging tools (e.g., Prometheus, Grafana, Loki, or Splunk). Security awareness: An understanding of platform security and software supply-chain practices. Bring your craft, curiosity and care for fellow developers. Together, we’ll build the foundations that help King teams create more moments of magic for players. About King With a mission of Making the World Playful, King is a leading interactive entertainment company for the mobile world with more than 20 years of history of delivering some of the world’s most iconic games in the mobile gaming industry, including the world-famous Candy Crush franchise, as well as other mobile titles such as Farm Heroes Saga. Around 200 million people play a King game every month. King, part of Microsoft (NASDAQ: MSFT), has Kingsters in Stockholm, Malmö, London, Barcelona, Berlin, Dublin, San Francisco, New York, Los Angeles and Malta. More information can be found at King.com or by following us on LinkedIn and @lifeatking on Instagram.
